verdict.rationale: Solid documents modular composition: components are plain functions and you are free to organize code as you like. It also ships Context as a built-in way to share state across the app, which is the framework's provider-style injection mechanism. However, the evidence never describes Context as dependency injection or explains provider/consumer scoping, so the DI half of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit docs on Context-based dependency injection (providers, scoping, consuming injected services), and hands-on corroboration of DI-style modular architecture.

support.subject: As a developer, I can organize my app into modular, dependency-injected building blocks

citations.quote: Performant state management is built-in with Context and Stores: you don't have to reach for a third party library to manage global state
In Solid, components are just functions - rendering is determined purely by how your state is used - so you're free to organize your code how you like
Provides modern framework features like JSX, fragments, Context, Portals, Suspense
